focus: OpenCode 2: hooks, tool names, install/update/rollback, compaction path, deny/rewrite/replace, subagent handling, project source, skills, v1 footprint

findings.claim: S-SKILLS in TECH-SPEC.md:212 and §9 marks 'does OpenCode expose a skill as a / command' as [U]. It is answerable from source now, and the answer is no: OpenCode 2 exposes a skill only as a model-called tool named `skill` (Input: {id}), not a slash command. This breaks the v2 plan in TECH-SPEC §3.9, which assumes the 3 context-mode skills (`/ctx-stats`, `/ctx-doctor`, `/ctx-upgrade`) are user-invoked slash commands with `disable-model-invocation: true` on every agent, including OpenCode 2.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/tool/plugin/skill.ts:10-24 (OpenCode clone, pinned `1438073`): `export const name = "skill"`; `Input = Schema.Struct({ id: Skill.ID... })`; description: 'Load a specialized skill's instructions ... when the task at hand matches its description. The skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.' There is no registration of a per-skill `/name` command anywhere in `packages/core/src/skill.ts` or `skill/discovery.ts` (both searched, grep for 'registerCommand', 'slash', '/\$' returns nothing). The model picks `id` itself; this is tool-gated skill loading, the same shape ADR-0004 says v2 avoids for routing text, but here applied to the 3 command skills themselves.
findings.archaeology: n/a for v1 (this is an OpenCode-2-source finding, not a context-mode v1 regression) — no ARCHAEOLOGY required since this does not change v1 behaviour, it closes an open spike with source evidence.
findings.fix: Resolve S-SKILLS for OpenCode 2 explicitly in TECH-SPEC §3.9: state that on OpenCode 2 the 3 skills are reachable only if the model decides to call the `skill` tool with a matching id, with no guaranteed user-typed `/ctx-stats` path. Either accept that gap in writing (same pattern as GS5's other per-agent carve-outs) or add instruction text telling the model when to call `skill` with these ids.

findings.claim: Pass A's opencode2-r4-2 confirms ADR-0016's claim that OpenCode 2 hooks run strictly in-process with no wire envelope, citing `packages/core/src/plugin/hooks.ts`. That file is real and matches, but the comment quoted ('Only tool execute.before may fail') describes the FAILURE channel, not whether a hook can REWRITE a tool's input/output — pass A's evidence does not actually show a rewrite/replace code path, only a failure-channel comment.
findings.evidence: packages/core/src/plugin/hooks.ts:18,23 (as quoted by pass A) defines `ToolHooks` and a failure-channel comment. The actual mutate-input-in-process / replace-result-in-process behaviour ADR-0016 claims is implemented in `packages/core/src/tool/plugin/skill.ts`-style tool wrapper code and the `Domains.tool` effect handler, not in `hooks.ts`'s type/comment alone. Pass A's finding is directionally correct (OpenCode 2 is in-process, confirmed by the Plugin.effect `ctx.tool.transform` pattern seen in skill.ts:33-35) but cites the wrong evidence line for the specific rewrite/replace mechanism.
findings.archaeology: n/a - evidence-precision correction to a prior pass A finding, not a new regression claim.
findings.fix: If ADR-0016's in-process rewrite/replace row for OpenCode 2 is cited again, point at the `ctx.tool.transform`/editor.add pattern (e.g. `tool/plugin/skill.ts:33-36`) rather than `plugin/hooks.ts`'s failure-channel comment, so the citation actually supports the rewrite claim.

findings.claim: GS3/G25 asks whether MCP-tool hooks fire on OpenCode 2, and ADR-0008 row 4 already answers 'in-process, availability is known' for Pi/OpenCode 2 readiness — but no v1 history exists for an OpenCode hooks.ts file at all (only a generic 2026 commit '75ae6ae3 feat: multi-platform adapters, session continiuty, hook scripts' touches it), so the planned GP-LIVE-HOOKS check for OpenCode 2 has no v1 prior art or regression baseline to compare against.
findings.evidence: `git log --follow --oneline -- src/adapters/opencode/hooks.ts` in cm-main (2230 commits) returns a single bulk commit `75ae6ae3` with no OpenCode-specific hook fix history (unlike Gemini/Codex/general hooks, which have many targeted fixes: #1222, #960, #529 etc. cited elsewhere in TECH-SPEC §3.8). There is no OpenCode-specific hook bug to carry forward as a SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINT, which is itself useful: it means G25 for OpenCode 2 is genuinely new ground, not a case where v2 risks re-breaking a known v1 fix.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 75ae6ae3 (bulk 'multi-platform adapters, session continuity, hook scripts' commit, no single issue/PR cited in the subject). ORIGINAL_INTENT: establish hook scripts across adapters generically, OpenCode included as one of several. REGRESSION_RISK: low for OpenCode specifically (no targeted fix history to re-break), but this also means the v2 team cannot lean on past OpenCode hook bugs to write GP-LIVE-HOOKS test cases -- those cases must be designed fresh. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: none inherited from v1; GS3 should state that OpenCode 2 hook-firing is an unverified, no-precedent claim, not merely '[U] test later'.
findings.fix: Note in TECH-SPEC §9 (G25 row) that OpenCode 2 has no v1 hook-fix history to validate against, so GP-LIVE-HOOKS for OpenCode 2 needs purpose-built test cases rather than regression replays of old issues.
